summary: Redwood AE/SE walked NovaRetail through Optimize quantization profiles (INT8 and FP8), demonstrated quality vs latency tradeoffs, and proposed a pilot. Customer cares about 2x cost reduction without >2% quality regression and predictable latency for 99th pct. Agreed next steps: provide dataset, run pilot evals, share pricing and security docs.
topics: quality vs latency comparisons and plots
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we can start in a minute, greetings.
00:08 Kevin Liu: yep good to go, thanks Maya.
00:12 Maya Chen: cool, i'm maya from Redwood, and with me is ethan park our solutions engineer. Quick agenda: demo of Optimize quant profiles - INT8 and FP8, show quality vs latency, and propose pilot.
00:28 Ethan Park: hi all, i'll jump into the profiler and the benchmark results. Quick note on transcription - some acronyms might appear funny, FP8 sometimes shows up as 'F P eight' in auto captions.
00:40 Samir Rao: sounds good, our main goal is reduce token cost and keep latency under 350ms p95 for web queries. We also want to keep quality hit <~2% if possible.
00:52 Lisa Gomez: and full SOC2/ISO audits are a hard requirement for production. We'll need KMS/HSM for keys.
01:02 Maya Chen: totally, we'll share security docs; Redwood Private and Dedicated options support KMS integrations.
01:12 Ethan Park: ok jumping in - here's a slide i sent earlier, but live view: we have three profiles in Optimize: baseline FP32, INT8 profile, and FP8 profile. The INT8 is more aggressive quant, gives biggest perf uplift on Ampere/4x GPUs; FP8 tends to preserve more quality while still giving nice latency drops.
01:31 Ethan Park: show of hands, do you run long form summarization or short Q/A?
01:36 Samir Rao: mostly Q/A and product description generation, average context ~512 tokens, responses ~80 tokens.
01:43 Ethan Park: great - that profile favors INT8 normally for cost, but FP8 can be a sweet spot if you need tighter quality.
01:51 Maya Chen: i'll share the benchmark spreadsheet after the call - it has raw token-level latencies and generation diffs.
02:02 Kevin Liu: how do you measure "quality" in these reports? Are these perf metrics or semantic similarity?
02:09 Ethan Park: good q - we use a suite: n-gram overlap (ROUGE-lite), embedding cosine similarity to reference, and some human eval buckets for edge cases. For NovaRetail we'd map them to your KPIs - e.g., product attribute extraction accuracy.
02:27 Samir Rao: do you support KV cache across quantized models? we've seen token regen regressions when cache is disabled.
02:34 Ethan Park: yes, KV cache is supported; small gotcha is some earlier quant pipelines needed cache warmup, but current runtime preserves cache and does prefix caching. Sometimes the transcript reads it as K-V cache, or K V cache.
02:48 Lisa Gomez: any special infra for FP8? we run on GCP A2 and some T4s for cost.
02:55 Ethan Park: FP8 works best on newer HW - we tested on H100 and A100, also Ampere family. On T4 you can do INT8 but FP8 isn't always fully supported unless you have transformer kernels compiled for fp8 paths. We can route requests to a compatible pool.
03:13 Maya Chen: let's look at a sample benchmark - here's latency vs quality chart (shared).
03:18 Ethan Park: baseline FP32 p50 ~120ms p95 ~490ms for this model and sequence length. INT8 profile brings p95 down to ~270-300ms, FP8 to ~330-360ms with lower quality delta.
03:30 Samir Rao: interesting - so INT8 gives ~45% p95 improvement but what about accuracy?
03:36 Ethan Park: typically on our retail QA dataset we saw INT8 avg quality drop ~1.8-2.5% depending on metric; FP8 was ~0.6-1.2%. There's variance by prompt shape.
03:49 Kevin Liu: if our SLA is p95 <350ms, INT8 might be the only one that guarantees it at scale?
03:55 Ethan Park: depends on batching and request mix. With Redwood Optimize autoscaling and batching knobs you can hit p95 <350 on FP8 for many workloads, but INT8 gives more headroom and lower cost.
04:10 Maya Chen: there's also cache and continuous batching impacts - if you have many similar prefixes, effective latency drops substantially.
04:18 Samir Rao: can you show the per-token cost estimate?
04:22 Ethan Park: sure, looking at cost model: FP32 baseline $0.12/token (example), INT8 $0.045/token, FP8 $0.06/token - numbers illustrative; real pricing varies by model and region.
04:36 Lisa Gomez: those numbers help - we target 2x cost reduction over current vendor.
04:41 Ethan Park: you should be able to hit ~2x with INT8 in many cases.
04:46 Speaker 1: (inaudible)
04:50 Maya Chen: i'll pause on slides and do a quick demo in the console - Optimize page, quant profiles.
04:57 Ethan Park: live console: here's profile selector, you can toggle INT8/FP8 and run quick evals against your prompt sets. There's a compare view with delta chart.
05:12 Samir Rao: I see a "regression threshold" slider - how strict should that be?
05:16 Ethan Park: we normally set regression alerts at 1.5% for canaries and 2.5% for full rollouts; you can customize. The system will auto-fall back to baseline on significant regressions.
05:29 Kevin Liu: about canaries - do you do traffic split and auto rollback?
05:33 Ethan Park: yes, canary deploys with A/B traffic split; we monitor quality and latency; if regression occurs above threshold we automatically shift traffic back.
05:42 Samir Rao: what's the effort for us to run the pilot? how long does it take to get reliable numbers?
05:47 Maya Chen: typically 1-2 weeks of sample runs plus a couple days for analysis; for NovaRetail given your dataset size we estimate 3-5 days to collect stable metrics.
05:58 Lisa Gomez: security timeline - we need SOC2 evidence and pen test up front for Dedicated/private.
06:05 Maya Chen: we'll send SOC2 report and pen test summary; Dedicated also supports customer-managed keys.
06:12 Ethan Park: switching back to quant - one more nuance: FP8 is less deterministic across some token patterns, so you'll see outliers in tail latencies sometimes; caching/kv workarounds mitigate this.
06:28 Samir Rao: can we run the pilot on our cluster? we have a dev cluster in GCP.
06:32 Ethan Park: yes, Redwood Private or Dedicated can be deployed to your VPC; for pilot we usually route requests through a test Dedicated pool and run the same traffic shape.
06:42 Maya Chen: action item: samir to share 5k prompts and target metrics, ethan will run INT8/FP8 and return full logs.
06:51 Samir Rao: noted.
06:55 Ethan Park: quick demo of eval output - shows per-prompt delta, cosine sims, and human-tagged buckets where FP8 handles synonyms better in a few cases.
07:08 Kevin Liu: any surprises in the earlier tests you ran? failures, hallucinations?
07:12 Ethan Park: some edge-case hallucinations increased slightly with INT8, which is why we recommend canary + regression sets. FP8 reduced those regressions but wasn't free.
07:24 Lisa Gomez: what's the difference in memory footprint? can we run more concurrent replicas with INT8?
07:29 Ethan Park: INT8 halves the model footprint roughly vs FP32, allowing more replicas per GPU, so concurrency improves and unit costs drop. FP8 reduces more subtly depending on kernel support.
07:41 Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
07:44 Maya Chen: on the console you can pin profiles per-route - so high-value routes can stay FP32 or FP8 while lower-cost routes go INT8.
07:56 Samir Rao: nice, that fits our mixed-criticality plan.
08:00 Ethan Park: i'll show a sample rollout config: start 5% traffic INT8, monitor 24-48h with regression sets, then move to 25, 50, 100. Auto-fallback on regression.
08:14 Samir Rao: do you expose raw latencies per token for our engineers?
08:18 Maya Chen: yes, the Console exposes token-level lat and cost, and traces for slow requests. You can export CSVs.
08:25 Lisa Gomez: about billing - how is pilot billed? usage-based or fixed?
08:29 Maya Chen: pilots can be usage-based with a credit, or a short-term dedicated commit if you want reserved capacity; we'll include options in the pricing doc.
08:38 Kevin Liu: any regulatory issues with PII in prompts? we scrub logs?
08:42 Ethan Park: we support redaction and partial log retention for Private and Dedicated. On hosted we have retention controls and can route through your KMS.
08:52 Samir Rao: one more technical q - do you support mixed precision where certain layers stay FP32?
08:57 Ethan Park: yes, mixed-precision profiles are possible; Optimize can create hybrid profiles where sensitive layers remain FP32 and others quantized; this reduces regressions.
09:10 Maya Chen: circling back - recommended for NovaRetail: pilot with INT8 for lower-cost routes, FP8 for customer-facing critical routes; run 1-week pilot, measure with your regression set.
09:22 Samir Rao: sounds fair. who will run the pilot?
09:25 Maya Chen: Ethan will run the evals and coordinate infra; Maya will send docs and pricing; Samir will provide prompt set and quality targets.
09:33 Kevin Liu: about SLA - what kind of guarantees on latency for Dedicated?
09:37 Maya Chen: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll include the numbers in the contract.
09:44 Lisa Gomez: can you also include a fail-open fallback if Dedicated nodes are saturated?
09:48 Ethan Park: yes, routing policies can failover to hosted lower-tier model or different region; we can configure that.
09:55 Speaker 3: (laughs).
09:57 Maya Chen: ok last items - i'll send a proposed pilot timeline: kickoff, dataset ingestion, baseline run, INT8/FP8 runs, analysis - total ~10 business days.
10:10 Samir Rao: timeline works.
10:13 Ethan Park: any blockers from your side?
10:16 Lisa Gomez: just security review and legal NDAs, we'll fast-track.
10:20 Maya Chen: perfect. We'll follow up with calendar invites.
10:24 Samir Rao: thanks all.
10:27 Maya Chen: thanks everyone, end of demo.
10:31 [end of recording]
